sampling_model.design: Known randomized second-stage audit within each dropout stratum, with a fixed bundle \(B_d\) and probability \(e_d(H_d)\).
sampling_model.units: Independent records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from the positive finite SCM class.
sampling_model.treatment: Observational treatment \(A\) has a strictly positive conditional law given \(W\); intervention replaces that kernel by \(A=a\).
sampling_model.overlap: All substantive table entries and all legal continuation and audit probabilities are strictly positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Use empirical observed-cell frequencies or Horvitz--Thompson audit-pattern tables with known \(e_d\); apply the returned finite reconstruction on a compatible regular branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Monotonicity permits several response-kernel recoveries yet a mediated self-censoring path makes the corresponding marginal and target laws nonidentified.
A categorical colluder propensity is identified if and only if its observable colluder matrices have full column rank.
Randomized intensive follow-up identifies and efficiently estimates smooth complete-data functionals when the phase-two variables complete the coarsened record.
In ordinary nonmonotone missing-data DAGs, absence of self-censoring and colluder obstructions characterizes full-law identification.
A sound intervention tree yields constructive target-law identification but is not complete.
Finite discrete causal queries admit sharp bounds through polynomial programming and convergent branch-and-bound.

body.tldr: Randomized recontact can identify a longitudinal intervention endpoint without recovering either the full missing trajectory or the endpoint among every audited dropout, but no existing theorem decides which partial measurement bundles suffice. The project seeks a finite interval-block certificate calculus for positive finite Markov chains with locally informative monotone hazards. Its central alternative returns either an evaluable endpoint reconstruction from dropout-indexed audit tables or two strictly positive graph-compatible SCMs with the same observed law and different endpoint intervention distributions. The resulting iff criterion generates the complete antichain of inclusion-minimal audit designs; plug-in Gaussian inference is derived on regular branches, and observed-cell projection gives finite-sample coverage on singular or nonidentified branches.

project_justification.gap: Passive monotone-MNAR theory supplies local recovery operations and a self-censoring-path obstruction, while randomized double-sampling theory assumes that phase two completes the missing record. Neither decides endpoint identification when each dropout stratum reveals only a fixed subset of future coordinates.
project_justification.niche: The local-parent Markov-chain restriction is narrow enough to expose interval boundaries and transport kernels, yet rich enough to exhibit deficient-rank concavity recovery, alphabet-sensitive identification, overlapping-bundle failure, and endpoint-only cancellation.
project_justification.fill: A constructive recovery-or-positive-obstruction calculus yields the exact graph-and-pattern criterion, an evaluable reconstruction, and every inclusion-minimal sufficient bundle design for arbitrary horizon.

body.related_work: Tikka and Karvanen (2025) show that deterministic monotonicity can rescue colluder structures and can create nonidentification along mediated self-censoring paths; their Discussion explicitly leaves a complete monotone criterion open. Tikka and Karvanen (2024) derive categorical colluder equations whose full-column-rank condition is necessary and sufficient for their full-law propensity target, motivating but not resolving the present positive rank strata. Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) characterize full-law identification for ordinary nonmonotone missing-data DAGs through an odds-ratio construction that cannot be evaluated on forbidden monotone patterns. Guo and Nabi (2026) track selection-bias propagation through a constructive intervention tree, but state that the algorithm is sound rather than complete and does not incorporate restrictions on the substantive law. Levis et al. (2024) identify smooth complete-data functionals after randomized intensive follow-up when phase two recovers the entire missing complement; a fixed bundle in this project may leave both an endpoint and another hazard parent unmeasured. Duarte et al. (2024) provide a polynomial-program oracle for each fixed finite instance, which is used for bounded verification and projected confidence sets rather than as the graph-explicit arbitrary-horizon criterion. Karvanen and Tikka (2024) and Bhattacharya et al. (2019) establish that target-law recovery need not coincide with full-law recovery, supporting the endpoint-specific state carried by the proposed calculus.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The load-bearing interval-block alternative and its positive obstruction-gluing theorem are open. The first rule system must recover the complementary-audit strict-concavity case and the binary bridge case, and it must reject the supplied four-visit overlapping-bundle counterexample. The exhaustive comparison over all \(1024\) designs for that fixed four-visit graph is an early kill test. A rule set that fails this audit must be abandoned or enlarged before an arbitrary-horizon induction. Generic real quantifier elimination, numerical fiber searches, and the finite polynomial confidence computation do not satisfy the identification theorem.
body.honest_scope: The proposal claims no completed arbitrary-horizon criterion. Exact audit-table equivalence, the local tail factorization, the single-hazard frontier, the complementary-audit concavity mechanism, the binary-versus-larger bridge boundary, and explicit positive counterexamples provide verified proof architecture that must be re-established in the paper. The open content is the exhaustive block state, every positive rank branch, endpoint-only cancellations, termination, and graph-compatible positive gluing. As sanity reductions, empty audit bundles must reproduce passive identification exactly when every local hazard uses only lagged states; auditing \(X_T\) in every dropout stratum must identify the endpoint by summing strata; and the certificate must reproduce the stated single-hazard proposition. No shadow-variable rank, parametric selection, missing-at-random, or faithfulness restriction is imposed. No polynomial-time guarantee is claimed.
